paper: NL2Bash: A Corpus and Semantic Parser for Natural Language Interface to the Linux Operating System (Lin et al.)
main_result: best top-1 full-command accuracy ~36%, template accuracy ~49-53%
limitation: single-reference scoring undercounts valid paraphrases; narrow ~100-utility domain; argument-filling much harder than structure prediction
relevance_to_termassist: Base/historical paper for this research program; TermAssist reframes the task as closed-set retrieval rather than open generation

paper: NLC2CMD Competition Report (Agarwal et al., NeurIPS 2020 competition track)
main_result: winning accuracy ~0.53 vs Tellina baseline 0.138 under a custom utility+flag-overlap metric
limitation: metric ignores literal arguments entirely; no team submitted a pure lexical-IR baseline (a gap TermAssist's BM25 baseline partially fills)
relevance_to_termassist: Establishes the standard eval protocol (utility+flag overlap) that is more compatible with retrieval-style near-miss answers than raw exact match

paper: Project CLAI: Instrumenting the Command Line as a New Environment for AI Agents (Agarwal et al.)
main_result: establishes IR-style retrieval as a legitimate fielded 'skill' alongside neural generation
limitation: infrastructure paper, not a benchmark
relevance_to_termassist: Precedent for treating lexical retrieval as a first-class, deployable approach rather than a naive baseline. Not re-verified in T6 (not cited)

paper: InterCode: Standardizing and Benchmarking Interactive Coding with Execution Feedback (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2023 D&B)
main_result: shows execution-feedback loops improve task completion over single-shot generation
limitation: requires live execution environment; LLM-agent-centric, doesn't apply to a non-LLM retrieval system directly
relevance_to_termassist: Motivates TermAssist's own functional evaluation (Phase 10) as the retrieval-appropriate analogue of execution-grounded eval. Not re-verified in T6 (not cited)

paper: Execution-Based Evaluation of Natural Language to Bash and PowerShell for Incident Remediation (Vo, Paulovicks, Sheinin, arXiv 2405.06807)
dataset: IBM Instana incident-derived categories; 125 hand-crafted test cases in three suites
model: seven closed and open-source LLMs, zero-shot and few-shot
main_result: argues surface-form metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, exact/partial match) are weak correctness proxies; proposes an execution-based evaluation platform
limitation: narrow industry domain (IT incident remediation); preprint
relevance_to_termassist: Directly supports TermAssist's Phase 10 rationale: exact-match alone is insufficient. Metadata and abstract checked 2026-09-28 (arXiv 2405.06807); not in references.bib

paper: LLM-Supported Natural Language to Bash Translation / NL2SH (Westenfelder et al., NAACL 2025)
dataset: NL2SH-ALFA: 600 manually verified test pairs, 40,939 training pairs
main_result: functional-equivalence heuristic judges equivalence with 95% confidence (+16% over previous heuristics); parsing, in-context learning, in-weight learning and constrained decoding improve NL2SH accuracy by up to 32% (abstract). [T6: an earlier version of this cell quoted accuracy that "remains low"; that quote could not be verified and was removed]
limitation: the equivalence heuristic itself uses an LLM and is imperfect
relevance_to_termassist: Modern generation-based successor to NL2Bash; TermAssist is NOT directly comparable (retrieval over closed set vs. open generation). Verified 2026-09-28 (ACL Anthology 2025.naacl-long.555)

paper: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures (Li, Zhang, Tresp, Yang)
task: evaluation methodology for LLM-issued shell commands
main_result: matched execution scores alone cannot distinguish generation errors from post-generation transport/parsing failures; replaying the same reply through an added parser lowers success by 55.4-73.2 points (abstract)
limitation: small benchmark (56 tasks); LLM-agent-specific failure mode (serialization/reparsing) not directly applicable to a closed-vocabulary retrieval system; preprint
relevance_to_termassist: Supports TermAssist's 'evaluation beyond exact match' theme (Phase 10/13). Abstract re-checked 2026-09-28 (arXiv 2608.13547)

paper: BashCoder-R1: Towards Robust and Explainable Bash Script Generation with Robustness-Aware GRPO
main_result: SyntaxPass ~95-100%, FuncRate ~93%, FullRate ~73-90% depending on task type
limitation: requires RL training infrastructure and a capable base LLM; not applicable to a no-LLM-constraint project
relevance_to_termassist: Modern (2026) LLM-based generation SOTA reference point; shows even strong generation systems report functional pass rates well under 100%, reinforcing that TermAssist's closed-retrieval framing (100% gold executability in Phase 10, by construction) is a different, more conservative trade-off, not a worse one

paper: BM25 Wins at Scale: A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms
model: BM25 vs dense vs hybrid retrievers
main_result: BM25 overtakes dense/hybrid methods at larger corpus scale, margin approaching 20 points at full scale
limitation: results are corpus-scale-dependent; TermAssist's corpus (431 commands) is far smaller than the regime studied
relevance_to_termassist: Directly supports positioning BM25 as a legitimate, non-naive retrieval choice, though TermAssist's corpus is much smaller than this paper's scaling regime -- cited for the general lexical-retrieval-competitiveness argument, not a scale-matched comparison

paper: An Empirical Study of Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation: Challenges and Opportunities
main_result: evaluates 5 retrieval algorithms including BM25 alongside neural code-search models
limitation: code-generation-augmentation framing, not command-retrieval-as-the-answer framing (TermAssist retrieves the final answer, not context for a generator)
relevance_to_termassist: Methodological precedent for BM25-vs-dense-vs-hybrid comparison in a code-adjacent domain; supports TermAssist's Phase 3/4/5 experimental design

paper: CodeSearchNet (Husain et al.)
dataset: ~2M functions across 6 languages, NL-docstring to code
main_result: establishes MRR/NDCG ranking-metric evaluation as standard for code retrieval; BM25 competitive baseline
limitation: general code search, not shell-command-specific
relevance_to_termassist: Standard reference for retrieval evaluation methodology (ranking metrics beyond top-1) that TermAssist's benchmark (Phase 7 AUROC/risk-coverage) follows in spirit

paper: Command-line Risk Classification using Transformer-based Neural Architectures (Notaro, Haeri, Cardoso, Gerndt)
dataset: realistic dataset of production commands (sizes previously recorded here as 71K GitHub Bash scripts + 47K labeled production commands; not in the abstract, not re-checked in T6)
model: transformer-based classifier using transfer learning from LLMs
main_result: transformer classifier for command risk, aimed at identifying rare dangerous commands; also applied to command interception and auditing rule-based systems (abstract)
limitation: requires a trained transformer model; the abstract argues rule-based systems need constant expert revision
relevance_to_termassist: TermAssist's safety classifier deliberately takes the rule-based, deterministic path this paper argues against; state the trade-off (auditability vs. coverage of unseen commands). Abstract re-checked 2026-09-28 (arXiv 2412.01655)

paper: how2 (Santinic, OSS tool, not peer-reviewed)
main_result: real-world precedent for retrieval-over-generation CLI assistance
limitation: no formal benchmark or accuracy figures published
relevance_to_termassist: Closest real-world precedent for TermAssist's retrieval-first philosophy, but unvalidated quantitatively -- cited for motivation, not comparison

paper: Explainshell (Kamara, OSS tool, not peer-reviewed)
main_result: purely lexical, non-ML precedent for CLI assistance
limitation: explains a command the user already has rather than retrieving one from an NL query
relevance_to_termassist: Sibling non-LLM CLI tool precedent supporting the 'lexical/deterministic tooling is a legitimate design space' argument

paper: whatisit-nl2sh (ThorOdinson246, OSS project)
model: fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, quantized, local CPU inference (~1s)
main_result: demonstrates a small local LLM can run offline on CPU for this task
limitation: not peer-reviewed; no published benchmark numbers
relevance_to_termassist: Relevant counterpoint: shows a *local* LLM is technically feasible for this task, which TermAssist deliberately does not adopt per its no-LLM-feature constraint -- worth citing in Limitations/Future Work as 'a path not taken, and why'

paper: An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction / CLINC150 (Larson et al., EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019)
task: closed-set intent classification with out-of-scope queries
dataset: 150 intents over 10 domains plus out-of-scope queries
model: benchmark classifiers with several out-of-scope identification schemes
main_result: classifiers do well on in-scope intents but struggle to identify out-of-scope queries (abstract)
limitation: dialog-assistant domain, not commands
relevance_to_termassist: Closest task framing to TermAssist: closed vocabulary plus rejection of out-of-scope requests; supports treating OOD rejection as a first-class metric. Verified 2026-09-28 (ACL Anthology D19-1131)

paper: Confidence Modeling for Neural Semantic Parsing (Dong, Quirk, Lapata, ACL 2018)
model: seq2seq parser plus a learned confidence model
main_result: a learned confidence model beats the posterior-probability baseline at predicting correctness (abstract)
limitation: generative parser; confidence features are model-internal
relevance_to_termassist: Precedent for predicting whether an NL-to-program output is correct from several uncertainty features, as TermAssist's hybrid reliability score does for retrieval. Verified 2026-09-28 (ACL Anthology P18-1069)

paper: Calibrated Interpretation: Confidence Estimation in Semantic Parsing (Stengel-Eskin, Van Durme, TACL 2023)
main_result: T6 saw only the title and a search summary; read the paper before citing it for any specific claim
limitation: generative; not retrieval
relevance_to_termassist: Establishes calibration of NL-to-program systems as an ACL/TACL topic. Metadata verified 2026-09-28 (Crossref 10.1162/tacl_a_00598); content NOT yet read

paper: Confidence Estimation for Error Detection in Text-to-SQL Systems (Somov, Tutubalina, AAAI 2025)
task: selective prediction and calibration for text-to-SQL
model: T5, GPT-4, Llama 3 with entropy-based selective classifiers
main_result: T5 better calibrated than GPT-4 and Llama 3; the selective classifier mostly catches irrelevant questions rather than wrong SQL (abstract)
limitation: LLM generation
relevance_to_termassist: Parallel to the T2 finding: confidence-based rejection mainly catches off-topic requests, not near-miss errors. Verified 2026-09-28 (Crossref 10.1609/aaai.v39i23.34699)

paper: What Predicts Correctness in Text-to-SQL? A Selective-Prediction Study (Richardson, arXiv 2026)
task: correctness prediction and abstention for text-to-SQL
model: LLM generators; self-consistency, log-probability and LLM-judge signals
main_result: black-box signals reach about 0.61-0.68 correctness AUROC; a two-provider LLM-judge ensemble reaches 0.82 (abstract)
limitation: single-author preprint, not peer-reviewed; LLM-based
relevance_to_termassist: Context for TermAssist's correctness AUROC (0.86 / 0.89), but a different task and difficulty, so NOT a like-for-like comparison. Metadata verified 2026-09-28 (arXiv 2607.06799); deliberately not added to references.bib

paper: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift (Kamath, Jia, Liang, ACL 2020)
task: selective QA on mixed in-domain and out-of-domain questions
dataset: SQuAD plus five other QA datasets
model: SQuAD-trained QA model plus a trained calibrator
main_result: a trained calibrator answers 56% of questions at 80% accuracy vs. 48% using softmax probability (abstract)
limitation: QA, not commands
relevance_to_termassist: Closest methodological precedent for TermAssist's learned hybrid reliability score used for abstention under OOD. Verified 2026-09-28 (ACL Anthology 2020.acl-main.503)

paper: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks (Geifman, El-Yaniv, NeurIPS 2017) and Bias-Reduced Uncertainty Estimation for Deep Neural Classifiers (Geifman, Uziel, El-Yaniv, ICLR 2019)
task: selective classification; risk-coverage; AURC and E-AURC
main_result: define the risk-coverage framework and the AURC / excess-AURC metrics that T3 reports
limitation: vision-only experiments
relevance_to_termassist: Method citations for T3. Verified 2026-09-28 (NeurIPS proceedings; arXiv 1705.08500, 1805.08206)

paper: Overcoming Common Flaws in the Evaluation of Selective Classification Systems (Traub et al., NeurIPS 2024)
main_result: argues that current multi-threshold metrics, including AURC, fail stated requirements; proposes AUGRC, which changes metric rankings on 5 of 6 datasets (abstract)
limitation: medical/vision focus
relevance_to_termassist: REVIEWER RISK for T3: the headline selective-prediction result uses AURC. T14 should cite this and either also report AUGRC or justify AURC. Verified 2026-09-28 (NeurIPS proceedings; arXiv 2407.01032)

paper: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks (Hendrycks, Gimpel, ICLR 2017)
task: OOD and error detection from maximum softmax probability
main_result: maximum-softmax confidence is a simple baseline for detecting errors and OOD inputs (abstract)
relevance_to_termassist: Method citation for using a confidence score as the OOD/error detector and reporting AUROC. Verified 2026-09-28 (arXiv 1610.02136)
